content: PanoRef multi-origin optimizer review and follow-up: A code review rated the algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, and readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, concluding the feature is promising but not production-ready. Strengths include deterministic area-proportional sampling, joint-pair search that ranks by bitset union with quality/contribution tie-breakers, and a shared coarse-to-fine engine (4,096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24,576 fine). Blockers identified: (1) imported sets can yield zero legal candidates because candidate clearance uses per-object AABBs, so origins inside a room enclosing AABB are rejected; fix is actual geometry clearance via coverage BVH point-to-triangle distance/sphere intersection, with per-mesh or clustered obstacle bounds and a regression test. (2) Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports: per-triangle expanded world-space arrays, JS objects/64-bit numbers, structured-clone into worker, and temporary array allocations during raycasts cause memory/GC pressure; fix is compact typed arrays (Float32Array positions/indices/normals, Uint32Array meshRanges/transforms), transferable ArrayBuffers, and a flat BVH or three-mesh-bvh, avoiding per-triangle vertex expansion. (3) Geometry extraction still blocks the main thread because extractCoverageScene runs synchronously before worker post; extraction should move into the worker or be chunked/yielding. (4) UI workflow 'Apply to selected panorama pair' rewrites existing panorama origins via updatePanoReference, which is wrong because panoramas are rendered from their original origin; correct workflow preserves existing panoramas, moves capture origins, renders new graybox panoramas, inprints/styles them, imports as new references, and associates each with its actual origin. (5) Reachable upper bound is mathematically inconsistent: reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates, while final combined coverage uses a different fine bank generated with seed+1, so UI can show combined > reachable; also fixed-first reachable set excludes the fixed first origin. Fix is one common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, and efficiency, and include fixed origin in reachable union for fixed-first. (6) Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation; rankSecondOrigins filters only by object identity, so identical/near-duplicate positions can survive; add distance(first, candidate) >= minimumOriginSeparation. Important refinements: 'four-level refinement' is not truly iterative—it generates offsets around the original seed at ±spacing/2, /4, /8, /16 without re-centering after each level; local candidates can float between floors because validation only checks that a floor exists somewhere below and offsets retain original Y, so on sloped/multilevel sets origins can float above a lower floor; fix is for each offset find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then clear. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules: optimizer evaluates angle and texel density, but shader blends only by distance, so optimized and visible results can diverge; shader should use same approximate quality function and winner-takes-most selection. Testing assessment: current unit tests are good but lack dangerous cases—large imported object containing a room, 100k+ triangle performance fixture, reachableCoverage >= combinedCoverage invariant, fixed-first candidate separation, sloped/multilevel floors, immutable existing panorama origins, candidate generation inside concave imported geometry; no GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head, so test suite not independently enforced in CI. Bottom line: preserve high-level design; required changes are replace AABB clearance with geometry clearance, replace object-heavy triangle/BVH data with typed arrays and transferable buffers, move extraction into worker, remove ability to relocate existing panorama references, recalculate reported metrics on one common sample bank, enforce separation in fixed-first, reproject local refinement candidates onto their floor. After those, optimizer would be strong; currently it should work on ordinary PanoRef primitive sets but is most likely to fail on complex imported production sets. Follow-up directive: rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict; add allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering; run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add a full 100K+ optimizer integration test (not just BVH-construction test); then spawn a subagent tasked to disprove that the goal is fully complete, report remaining holes, fix them, and repeat until subagent finds no holes. Implementation actions taken: inspected projectedStyleMaterials.ts and multiOriginInteraction.test.ts; removed stale PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0 constant and old distance-only blend test; replaced with assertions guarding optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0 and == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0) and projectedQualityAt, and ensured projectedConfidence is not present; applied patch and ran targeted test (36 tests passed). Then ran full unit suite (371 tests passed across 42 files, including projectionCoverage engine test on 100k+ triangle fixture and WebGL projected-style compile/readback tests), lint (tsc --noEmit passed), and build (vite build passed).

PanoRef multi-origin coverage optimizer audit and follow-up: an independent adversarial audit disproved full completion on two points—(1) the rebased history is not yet published (GitHub reports CONFLICTING/DIRTY), and (2) imported-floor filtering still admits large disconnected props (a 6×6 floor plus a disconnected 3×3 tabletop returned all four triangles as legal floor triangles; current size thresholds cap at 8 m² and the test only covers a 1.4×1.4 tabletop). All other checks passed: typecheck, build, 81 targeted optimizer/multi-origin/WebGL tests, the full 101,250-triangle two-mode optimizer test, and real production-scene benchmark evidence. Prior review had rated architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, and readiness for complex imported sets 4/10, with blockers around per-object AABB clearance, object-heavy triangle/BVH data, synchronous main-thread extraction, UI rewriting existing panorama origins, reachable-coverage metric inconsistency, and missing fixed-first separation; implementation actions hardened coverage floors and rebased the candidate state (commit t3code/projector-occlusion ab5873a, 'Resolve multi-origin rebase and harden coverage floors', 18 files changed, 481 insertions, 216 deletions). Follow-up directive: add an explicit allowed-floor-region mechanism (so ambiguous large horizontal surfaces are user-constrained instead of guessed) plus the auditor's large-top regression, then publish only after that revision passes and a fresh auditor cannot find a hole; the candidate state is deliberately frozen underneath the still-running audit subagent.

The allowed-floor-region mechanism was implemented across the engine, UI, and tests: types gained `allowedFloorRegions?: CoverageBounds[]`, extraction normalizes and stores the regions, floor selection switches to region intersection when regions are present, and candidate generation rejects points outside the allowed bounds. The UI panel adds a toggle plus X/Y/Z min/max inputs and passes the region into extraction. A regression test builds a 6×6 floor plus a disconnected 3×3 top and asserts that an allowed region of ±3.1 around the origin keeps only the two floor triangles and yields candidates at y=1.6. Documentation strings in README.md and the regression audit were updated to describe connected-component filtering plus explicit allowed-floor bounds for ambiguous large tops. A first patch attempt failed because README.md already lacked the exact old line and because `Field` did not accept a `key` prop and the region cast was not narrowed to `Vec3`; those were fixed by removing the `key` props (wrapping in `<div key>`), casting `min`/`max` as `Vec3`, and re-applying. After the fixes, `tsc --noEmit` (lint) passed and the targeted test run (`projectionCoverage.test.ts`, `multiOriginInteraction.test.ts`, `uiFidelity.test.ts`) was initiated but the supplied evidence ends before its final pass/fail result is recorded. The base capsule’s two disproved completion points remain in force: the rebased history is not yet published (GitHub reports CONFLICTING/DIRTY) and imported-floor filtering still admits large disconnected props without the explicit allowed-region constraint; the candidate state is frozen under the still-running audit subagent and publication is gated on the auditor’s large-top regression passing and a fresh auditor finding no hole.

Round two audit found one concrete hole: allowed-floor controls remain editable during a running analysis, but edits do not cancel or invalidate the in-flight job, so the old result can appear under newly displayed bounds or after those bounds become invalid. All other criteria passed, including PR #23 MERGEABLE/CLEAN, local/remote heads matching and based on current origin/main, region constraints surviving worker transfer and covering generation/refinement paths, large-tabletop regression passing, full 101,250-triangle fixed-first and joint integration test passing, and real benchmark evidence remaining valid. The stale-result race is fixed by disabling the toggle and all six fields for the full running state, with a browser regression asserting the controls lock and unlock around the optimizer job; the fix is committed and pushed (commit 4153429, Lock coverage floor bounds during analysis), and adversarial audit round three is begun against that commit.

Round three audit found two stale-state holes: editing bounds after a completed run leaves the old result and origin-apply actions visible even when origins fall outside the newly displayed region, and changing the primary panorama does not refresh the untouched default region or invalidate a fixed-first result, leaving the region centered on the previous panorama. The in-flight locking fix itself works, and PR publication, ancestry, benchmark evidence, heavy integration test, worker/refinement constraints, docs, and verification remain sound. The fix centralizes result invalidation for every optimizer input and synchronizes only untouched default bounds to the active capture origin while preserving user-authored bounds; CoverageOptimizerPanel gains a defaultFloorRegion helper, a floorRegionTouchedRef, a captureInputKey, a previousCaptureInputKeyRef, and an invalidateAnalysis function, with mode/region/bound changes calling invalidateAnalysis and the bound inputs also setting floorRegionTouchedRef, plus a useEffect that invalidates and (when untouched) recenters default bounds on capture-origin/key/camera-height changes. A regression adds an e2e step filling the X floor minimum to -4 and asserting zero results and no apply-capture button. After the patch, lint (tsc --noEmit) passed, targeted tests passed (uiFidelity 40, multiOriginInteraction 36, projectionCoverage 11 = 87 tests; the 100k+ triangle projection coverage engine test ran in ~35.8s), build succeeded (vite, 8.31s; dist warning about a >500kB chunk), and the e2e coverage-optimizer-completes regression passed on desktop-chromium and phone-390. The fix was committed as 4f4fd39 ("Invalidate stale coverage optimizer results", 2 files, 72 insertions, 27 deletions) and pushed to t3code/projector-occlusion; gh pr view 23 reports headRefOid 41534294b0f5b67b82317c50a7060352576675c5, mergeStateStatus CLEAN, mergeable MERGEABLE, url https://github.com/distilledoreo/PanoRef/pull/23, with push updating 4153429..4f4fd39. Both round-three stale-state paths are fixed and published: completed results disappear immediately when any bound changes, and active panorama/capture inputs invalidate results while untouched default bounds recenter automatically; audit round four is begun.

Round four audit found one remaining cancellation hole: stale extraction failures bypass the analysis-identity check and can overwrite a newer analysis state with `failed`. The fix adds the same identity guard to the extraction catch and a regression test asserting both successful and failed coverage extraction paths guard against stale analysis identity. Verification: PR #23 is MERGEABLE/CLEAN; local and remote heads match current origin/main; bounds and capture-input changes invalidate successful results correctly; region enforcement covers worker, candidate, and refinement paths; heavy two-mode integration and real benchmark evidence remain valid; recorded typecheck, build, WebGL, browser, and workflow verification is intact. The regression test initially failed (expected 4 identity guards, got 2) before the patch was applied.

Audit round five found no remaining concrete holes. The stale extraction-failure path now checks analysis identity before mutating status, with a regression protecting both success and failure guards; the fix was committed and pushed as 80882e3 on t3code/projector-occlusion, rebased on current origin/main. PR #23 is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with latest Netlify checks passed. A final clean-head run passed 373/373 tests (including real WebGL pixel readback and the full 101,250-triangle optimizer) plus a 33.1 MB workflow export smoke; a documentation-only stale count in docs/ui-revamp-regression-audit.md was corrected from 303/303 to 373/373. Verification evidence remains intact: bounds/capture changes invalidate results correctly, region enforcement covers worker/candidate/refinement paths, heavy two-mode integration and real benchmark evidence remain valid, and recorded typecheck, build, WebGL, browser, and workflow verification is intact.

Final adversarial audit round six found no concrete holes on published HEAD c1f6c8d. PR #23 is MERGEABLE/CLEAN with all Netlify checks complete; the branch is synchronized locally and remotely on current origin/main. A documentation-only commit c1f6c8d corrected the recorded coverage verification count to 373/373 tests (42 files) with no runtime or configuration change. The temporary local Vite preview process used for browser verification was stopped. The goal is marked complete: rebase, occlusion/coverage implementation, 100K+ triangle optimizer integration, real imported-set benchmark, and all verification (typecheck, build, unit, WebGL, browser, workflow) remain satisfied across six audit rounds, with rounds five and six finding no remaining holes.
